svg.title: Metformin for longevity: what has actually been tested
svg.desc: Metformin for longevity: what has actually been tested. Regulatory status (US): Prescription drug for type 2 diabetes. Not approved to slow aging or extend life. Verdict: Not approved for aging. Lifespan in mice: One NIA lab study: longer life in males (2013). Multi-site NIA program: no significant gain alone (2016). Verdict: Mixed animal signal. Survival in people (observational): UK 2014: diabetics on metformin outlived matched non-diabetics. Denmark 2022, incl. twins: no. Verdict: Conflicting, not causal. Lifespan in people: No human trial has measured it. TAME, proposed in 2016, has no ClinicalTrials.gov record. Verdict: Not tested. Muscle and physical function, 65+: MASTERS: less muscle gain with training. MET-PREVENT, DEMFOS: main goals missed. Verdict: Mostly negative. Aging biomarkers: HIV trial missed its epigenetic-age goal; small trials report clock or telomere shifts. Verdict: Weak, mixed. Diabetes prevention: Cut new diabetes by 31% in the DPP (2002); lifestyle change cut it by 58%. Verdict: Proven, but not aging. Safety: Boxed warning for lactic acidosis; can lower vitamin B12; stomach side effects common. Verdict: Real drug risks.
